item.title: Ranji Trophy: Musheer Khan spins Mumbai to pole position
item.description: MUMBAI: Musheer Khan continues to make up for lost time after the serious car accident that sidelined him in Sept 2024. Producing a memorable allround performance that is bound to catch the eye of the national selectors, the 21-yearold became only the sixth Mumbai cricketer to score a century and claim a fivewicket haul in the same first-class match, putting Mumbai on the verge of their third outright win of the season in their Ranji Trophy Elite Group D clash against Haryana at the MCA ground in BKC on Wednesday. After making 109 at No. 3, the left-arm spinner returned figures of 6/85 from 31 overs, including seven maidens, as Haryana were bowled out for 270 in 107.5 overs and forced to follow on. At stumps, Haryana were 73 for 2 in their second innings, still 87 runs short of making Mumbai bat again. Before Musheer, only Madab Raiji, Dattu Phadkar, Vinoo Mankad, Polly Umrigar and Ravi Shastri had achieved the rare Mumbai double of a century and a five-for in the same first-class match. “I’ve been an allrounder from junior cricket. If I bat for an hour or an hour and ahalf in practice, I make sure I bowl around 120 deliveries too,” Musheer said. “I was actually a proper bowler when I was younger. I didn’t have much power in my batting then. At this level, though, it took me a couple of years to establish myself as abowler because we had senior bowlers.” Rain hurts Delhi’s chances In Ranchi, not a single ball was bowled on the third day of Delhi’s third round encounter against Jharkhand, which has effectively ended the visiting team’s chances of earning an outright win. Jharkhand were in a spot of bother at 131 for 4 at stumps on the second day after Delhi posted 515/5 declared. item.title: China deems Real Madrid’s apology insufficient over Mbappe’s statement and delivers firm response
item.description: China deems Real Madrid’s apology insufficient over Mbappe’s statement and delivers firm response Real Madrid are facing growing pressure to resolve the controversy surrounding Kylian Mbappe’s recent comments about China. What initially appeared to be an issue involving the Frenchman’s personal image has developed into a serious commercial and diplomatic concern for the club. According to Mundo Deportivo , Chinese state broadcaster China Media has rejected the explanations given by Real Madrid regarding the controversy. The broadcaster has insisted that the club must also accept responsibility for its player’s remarks. Chinese broadcaster sends strong message to Real Madrid The controversy began when Mbappe discussed his favourite internet meme during an interview, referring to an image featuring his face superimposed on that of former Chinese leader Mao Zedong. The broadcaster subsequently suspended La Liga coverage, including matches involving Mbappe, and removed promotional content featuring the Frenchman. The Mbappe situation has escalated out of control. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) CMG also rejected the argument that Mbappe had no intention of causing offence and was entitled to express his personal opinions. The organisation insisted that his comments went beyond the boundaries of freedom of expression and demanded a satisfactory apology from the Spanish giants. “Until Real Madrid presents an appropriate apology, there is nothing to discuss,” the broadcaster warned. Real Madrid respond with official apology Following the broadcaster’s criticism, Madrid issued an official statement on Wednesday, apologising for the discomfort caused by Mbappe’s remarks. The club expressed its respect for China’s history, culture and people, while supporting the apology Mbappe had already issued. CMG subsequently acknowledged receiving Madrid’s written apology through La Liga , although it did not confirm whether the suspended broadcasts would resume. Tebas has tried to pacify the situation through mediation channels. (Photo by Arnold Jerocki/Getty Images For Sportel) Meanwhile, three Chinese companies have already terminated their commercial agreements with Mbappe, highlighting the financial implications of the controversy. This is also set to affect Los Blancos , as the club holds a percentage of his image rights and stands to lose out on important revenue. The club’s decision to apologise demonstrates its willingness to protect those diplomatic relationships. However, the situation remains unresolved, and until broadcasts resume, this will remain on everyone’s mind. Madrid will hope that their official apology helps calm things down, and it remains to be seen how the situation plays out.

item.title: Josh Inglis, Alex Carey put Australia in control of third Test against South Africa
item.description: Josh Inglis and Alex Carey stitched together an unbeaten fifth-wicket partnership of 145 runs to put Australia in command of the deciding third Test against South Africa, taking the visitors to 330/4 at stumps on Day 2. Inglis remained unbeaten on 85 off with nine fours and two sixes, while Carey scored 51 not out as Australia edged past South Africa’s first-innings total of 329 in the final over of the day. Playing his first Test since December, Inglis led Australia's recovery in a dominant final session, during which the visitors added 139 runs without losing a wicket. Carey, meanwhile, registered his first half-century in 12 Test innings. The pair also recorded Australia's first century-plus fifth-wicket stand against South Africa since 2014. Earlier, Matt Renshaw scored 74 and Cameron Green contributed 65 to strengthen Australia's reply after a promising opening stand between Renshaw and Travis Head. The pair added runs comfortably before off-spinner Simon Harmer struck twice in the same over. Head was bowled for 41 after chopping the ball onto his stumps, while Marnus Labuschagne fell for a five-ball duck after edging to slip. Renshaw and Green then combined for a 126-run third-wicket partnership, taking Australia to 148/2 before lunch and continuing their stand into the afternoon session. Both batters brought up their half-centuries, with Green particularly aggressive against Kagiso Rabada. However, Marco Jansen swung the momentum back South Africa's way by dismissing both set batters within two overs. Renshaw was caught behind after attempting to attack a short delivery, with the decision confirmed by DRS. The wicket was Jansen's 100th in Test cricket. Green followed soon after, edging to slip. South Africa appeared to have regained control heading into the final session, but Inglis and Carey ensured Australia finished the day firmly on top. The three-match series is level at 1-1. Australia won the opening Test in Durban by 214 runs, while South Africa bounced back with an innings-and-31-run victory in Gqeberha. The third and final Test in Cape Town remains finely poised, with Australia holding the advantage after a strong batting display. 135295782

item.title: Five things to know about Ball State basketball before the 2026-27 season
item.description: College basketball season is looming large, and Ball State basketball is ready to begin a new era for the program. Ball State is coming off a 12-19 season which marked its third consecutive year finishing below .500 and missing the Mid-American Conference Tournament. The Cardinals' struggles led to a change in leadership as head coach Michael Lewis was fired after four seasons and replaced with Chris Capko , a first-year head coach. Capko will look to bring the Cardinals back to the postseason for the first time since 2023. More: Five things to know about Ball State women's basketball before 2026-27 season Ball State will tip off its 2026-27 season on the road at Georgia Southern on Monday, Nov. 2. Here are five things to know about Ball State basketball before the season begins. Who is the new coach for Ball State basketball? Capko was officially hired to lead the Ball State basketball program on March 20, becoming the 21st head coach in program history. He spent the last decade as an assistant coach under Andy Enfield with eight years at Southern California and the last two as the associate head coach at Southern Methodist. Prior to his time with Enfield, Capko also served as an assistant coach at Florida International, Georgia Southern, Stetson and Marshall. He also played four years of collegiate hoops as a point guard at South Florida from 2003-07. Capko also brought in a (mostly) new crop of assistant coaches. Pershin Williams joined the fold after spending the last three seasons as an assistant at Georgia Tech and also helped develop Kennesaw State into an NCAA Tournament team as an assistant coach there for four years. Jordan Surenkamp spent last season as an assistant at Radford and has a decade of experience as an NBA G-League coach. Manny Dosanjh brings some MAC experience to the table after spending the last four years as an assistant at Western Michigan and was highlighted as one of the top 100 most impactful assistant coaches in the nation by Silver Waves Media. Capko also welcomed in Beruk Asfaw as director of basketball operations and Ellis Spar as director of analytics and strategy. More: New coach Chris Capko is ready to lead Ball State basketball revival The lone holdover from last year's coaching staff is John Clancy. He joined the Cardinals in 2025 as an assistant on Lewis' staff and was retained by Capko for the 2026 season. He has previously served as an assistant coach at Western Illinois and as a head coach at Triton College. Who is returning for Ball State basketball? item.title: Lamar Jackson is back. Can he spark a Ravens victory over the Bills?
item.description: The Baltimore Ravens will be desperate for a victory against the Buffalo Bills this weekend coming off a humbling loss to the Cincinnati Bengals last week. The Ravens blew a 13-0 halftime lead and played a simply horrendous second half in their 35-13 defeat to AFC North rival Cincinnati. It got ugly in Baltimore as Cincinnati scored touchdowns on five straight possessions in the second half while the Tyler Huntley-led offense had zero response, netting just 87 yards after the intermission. Now the Ravens (4-3) go on the road to face a Bills team (5-1) coming off a bye. The Bills have faced a number of opponents (Chargers, Patriots, Raiders) this year coming off dispiriting losses. So if the Ravens are going to be a mad bunch Sunday, it will be nothing new for Buffalo in 2026. “In every game, we’ve proven that we’re good enough to be the type of team that we want to be, and we’ve proven that we’re bad enough to be a not very good team as well,” Ravens coach Jesse Minter said. “There’s a consistency level that we need to find, where it’s less riding the wave of momentum and more about staying even-keeled and finding a way to have each other’s back and finding a way to pick each other up. You can look at really all three phases in the second half of completely momentum-losing type of plays. That is what it is.” The biggest reason for optimism for the Ravens is the expected return of star quarterback Lamar Jackson, who missed the last three games with a high ankle sprain. Baltimore went 1-2 with backup Tyler Huntley taking snaps in Jackson's absence. So while it's better in Buffalo’s world than it is Baltimore’s right now, that could change in a hurry. item.title: Indiana football QB Josh Hoover listed as probable for Minnesota game
item.description: BLOOMINGTON — For the first time this season, Indiana football starting quarterback Josh Hoover found himself listed on the team's availability report. Hoover is listed as probable for the No. 4 Hoosiers (7-1, 4-1 Big Ten) ahead of a matchup against Minnesota. The designation isn't totally unexpected with IU coach Curt Cignetti telling reporters Hoover wasn't at 100% after a 13-6 overtime win over Michigan. The coaching staff considered replacing him with backup QB Grant Wilson with Hoover only attempting two passes after halftime. The injury stems from the awkward hit he took to his throwing arm in the Ohio State game. On Monday, Cignetti didn't sound worried about Hoover having to sit out. The fifth-year quarterback hasn't missed a start due to injury in his college career. "I expect him to be fine and better this week," Cignetti said. More: Indiana football QB Josh Hoover’s ‘dog mentality’ gives Hoosiers a winning edge While Hoover was limited in the second half against Michigan, the toughness he displayed making the key plays in overtime to help IU pull out a victory impressed his teammates. Hoover has thrown for 1,741 yards with 18 touchdowns and an interception this season. He has a 170.9 passer rating that ranks No. 12 among all FBS quarterbacks. “It's the dog mentality,” Indiana center Bray Lynch said on Tuesday night. “And if you asked me if he were to get hurt before the season started and played, I would have told you, 'Hell yeah, he would have.' He's a dog like that.” Hoover isn't alone on the injury report. Indiana listed wide receiver Davion Chandler and defensive end Kellan Wyatt as out and safety Quan Sanks as questionable. Wyatt, one of the many student-athletes fighting the NCAA's eligibility rules in court , suffered a lower body injury against Michigan. Thanks to his eligibility situation, he spent much of the offseason rehabbing the season-ending knee injury he suffered in 2025 on his own. He climbed up the depth chart in recent weeks to become the first defensive end off the bench behind Tobi Osunsanmi and Stephen Daley. He made the most of the opportunities with seven quarterback pressures over IU's last three games. Indiana still has plenty of depth at the position with Josh Burnham and Daniel Ndukwe likely in line to get more snaps. At receiver, Chandler has been in the mix alongside Tyler Morris and Shazz Preston as Indiana's third receiver. He's been the most productive of the group — he has 11 catches for 131 yards for four touchdowns — but Cignetti said that no one has been consistent enough in the spot. "Still kind of waiting for one guy to separate themselves," Cignetti said. Michael Niziolek is the Indiana beat reporter for The Bloomington Herald-Times. You can follow him on X @michaelniziolek . item.title: Will Rams hunt blockbuster trade after 49ers, Seahawks deals? Sean McVay weighs in
item.description: David Brytus-Imagn Images Will Rams hunt blockbuster trade after 49ers, Seahawks deals? Sean McVay weighs in appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Rams swung a huge trade in the offseason after acquiring Myles Garrett from the Cleveland Browns in exchange for Jared Verse and draft assets. It was viewed as a big win for the Rams . Unfortunately, Garrett suffered a knee injury in Week 1 , instantly derailing Los Angeles’ campaign. Amid his continued absence and the Rams’ 3-4 record, the front office could hunt for another blockbuster trade to salvage the season. Coach Sean McVay , however, is not keen on it, as reported by The Athletic’s Nate Atkins. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “No, that’s not something (we want). Based on our situation, what you look at is hopefully some of those trades will be guys getting back from injury that haven’t played for us. That’s the way that we look at it,” said McVay. “You always think about it, but with the amount of guys who have not been available, guys who are key and focal points on both sides of the football, we look at those guys hopefully being able to return within a month. That’s where that value lies for us. Maybe it’d be a different conversation if we’re talking about guys who are on injured reserve and done for the whole season. The good thing is, a lot of the guys who are huge parts that we’re missing, we do expect to get back at some point, just not exactly sure when that is.” The Seattle Seahawks and the San Francisco 49ers already acquired extra weapons ahead of the trade deadline. The Seahawks and the 49ers got Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, respectively, from the Indianapolis Colts, who received draft assets in return. Aside from Garrett, also out for the Rams are Davante Adams (hamstring injury), Trent McDuffie (groin injury), Kobie Turner (groin injury), Blake Gripe (ACL injury), and Terrance Ferguson (ankle injury), among others. The Rams will face the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday. item.description: Take a bow Austin Hough. The content coach had a perfect prediction record last week as he went 12-0 as the playoffs kicked off for Indiana high school football teams. And it's the kickoff of the state tournament series north of the border in Michigan as Edwardsburg, Niles and all Buchanan qualified for the postseason. The game to see Friday night maybe in the state happens in downtown South Bend. No. 9 Saint Joseph's will host No. 6 Northridge in a Class 4A clash of heavyweights on Father Bly Field in Leighton Stadium. The host Huskies moved to 9-1 by downing South Bend Riley at home 38-0 last week. The Raiders remained undefeated, moving to 10-0 by running past Mishawaka 57-26 in Middlebury thanks to a 21-0 edge in the fourth quarter. The game will be a matchup of the stingy St. Joe defense versus the prolific offense of the Raiders. The Huskies are allowing just 8.9 ppg. with a season high of 38 in a 38-7 loss at Class 6A No. 6 and undefeated Penn. St. Joe has three shutouts and have allowed double digits in points in just three games. The St. Joe defense is led by the likes of senior lineman Charlie Moran, senior defensive back James Criniti and senior Jack Kelly and sophomore Will Criniti at linebacker spots. The Northridge offense is propelled by star quarterback Jake Scholl. The unflappable, 6-2, 190-pound sophomore has thrown for 2,177 yards, while completing 68 percent of his throws with 25 touchdowns and six interceptions. Scholl has rushed for a team-high 954 yards on 126 carries with 23 more touchdowns. He had 266 total yards and six touchdowns last week in the romp over Mishawaka. item.title: Fastest expansion teams to win a championship: Where Valkyries would rank among quickest title winners in sports history
item.description: Fastest expansion teams to win a championship: Where Valkyries would rank among quickest title winners in sports history originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Two years ago, the Golden State Valkyries were nothing more than an idea of a franchise still being developed. They had their team name, a logo and a general manager, but in October 2024, the Valkyries didn't yet have a single player on their roster. Now, after just two seasons' worth of games, Golden State enters Thursday on the verge of becoming the WNBA's model franchise. With a 3-2 lead over the Dream entering Game 6 of the 2026 WNBA Finals, the Valkyries can secure their first-ever championship with one more win. Should Golden State close out the series — whether in six or seven games — the WNBA's 2025 expansion squad would be making North American professional sports history. Here's how a potential Valkyries championship would compare to the fastest title runs from an expansion franchise across other pro sports leagues. MORE: Why WNBA Finals Game 6 has unusual start time Fastest expansion teams to win a championship If the Valkyries close out the 2026 WNBA Finals with the trophy, they will be setting a new record for the fastest expansion team among the major North American sports leagues (NBA, WNBA, NHL, MLB, NFL) to win a title, doing so in just two seasons. Currently, the 1970-71 Milwaukee Bucks hold the record for the fastest championship by an expansion franchise. The Bucks' first NBA season was in 1968-69, and after drafting Kareem Abdul-Jabbar (then Lew Alcindor) in 1969, they proceeded to win the championship in their third season of existence. That span of just three seasons needed by the Abdul-Jabbar and Oscar Robertson-led Bucks to win a title has held up as the quickest turnaround by an expansion franchise. The only other expansion franchises from the major North American sports leagues to win a championship within five years are the 2001 Arizona Diamondbacks (first MLB season in 1998), the 2004 Seattle Storm (added to WNBA in 2000) and the 1997 Florida Marlins (first MLB season in 1993). In the NFL, while the Ravens were technically a continuation of the Cleveland Browns' franchise rather than an expansion team, they had the quickest turnaround from Year 1 as a team to a Super Bowl in 2000. item.title: Horses, farming and a bad injury - McNabney's rise to Ireland
item.description: James McNabney could make his Ireland debut in November's Nations Championship fixtures [Getty Images] "Will you ever be home to the farm again?" That was the light-hearted response from James McNabney's father after he was called into the Ireland squad for the first time. When the news came, the 23-year-old back row was in South Africa with Ulster and, without an eSIM in his phone, was trying to connect to WiFi when out for coffee. When finally online, he saw the email that said he had earned an Ireland call-up from Andy Farrell. "I was delighted. It was a big moment for the family as well," McNabney said. "My mum was very proud and I don't think my dad knew what way to take it at the start. "But no, they're both delighted for me and I appreciate the support they've given me." McNabney keen to show Ireland coaches 'what I'm all about' Ringrose set to miss Ireland's November games McNabney's route into the Ireland set-up is not the traditional path taken by most players. Growing up on a farm in Ballymena, he did not watch a lot of rugby growing up and only started playing in school. At the time, horses were his focus. Long before he had even dreamt of becoming a professional rugby player, he had represented Northern Ireland and Great Britain in equestrian. "I rode horses from probably when I was about six until I was 16," he said. "Horses was sort of a main hobby, then it became a sport for me." At 16 he was given an ultimatum over his sporting future. "Michael Black [a provincial talent coach] from Ulster was like, 'you need to make the decision whether you're going to put on a bit of timber and play rugby or stay lean and ride a horse'. "I decided to play rugby. I was enjoying it, I stuck at it and here I am." As for equestrian, there's no more horsing around for the big back row. "We've still got one at home. If I'm taken to the field then I'll maybe jump on it. "Other than that, I only do it for the craic. I haven't been on a horse in, I'd say, six months." Given his other interests, McNabney says he did not have a lot of rugby heroes growing up and instead simply "enjoyed playing it". "I didn't really watch it that much. That probably went against me because I was quite green, and didn't know much about it. "But it wasn't until I was getting to Ireland Under-20s that I really thought this is what I'm going to do for a job." 'There are going to be setbacks' Back row NcNabney made his return from an ACL injury for Ulster in pre-season [Getty Images] An Under-20 Six Nations Grand Slam winner in 2022 and 2023, McNabney's senior Ireland chance came more than a year later than he initially hoped. After an impressive season with Ulster, he had been included by Farrell as a training panellist for the 2025 Six Nations. He was set to be included again for the summer fixtures against Japan and Georgia when the bulk of the front-liners were away with the British and Irish Lions, but he did not get meet up with the squad after he sustained an ACL injury.

Speaking to talkSPORT , the Fleetwood goalkeeper explained the chaotic aftermath on the pitch. item.title: Brewers win first World Series in 57-year history
item.description: William Contreras and Milwaukee team-mates Jackson Chourio and Antonio Senzatela also helped Venezuela win the World Baseball Classic in March [Getty Images] The Milwaukee Brewers have won the World Series for the first time in the franchise's 57-year history. They beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in game five in Florida on Wednesday to clinch a 4-1 win in the best-of-seven Fall Classic. The Brewers, whose only previous appearance in the World Series came in 1982, are based in Major League Baseball's smallest market and this year had the 19th highest payroll of its 30 teams. But for the second straight year, the Brewers finished the regular season with MLB's best record and they then proved their class with a dominant run in the play-offs. They avenged last season's loss to the Los Angeles Dodgers in the National League Championship Series by sweeping the two-time defending champions. That secured a spot in the 123rd World Series, where the Brewers became MLB champions with 11 wins from 13 games in the postseason. Milwaukee's William Contreras was named the World Series' most valuable player, with the 28-year-old becoming the eighth catcher to win the award and the third Venezuelan. The Brewers won the first two games in Wisconsin and then the first in Florida, before the Rays, who were the American League's top seed, took it to game five. Milwaukee went ahead at the top of the second inning as a single from Cooper Pratt sent Brice Turang home, before they added another run in the fifth off a David Hamilton hit. The Brewers doubled their lead in their next at-bat through a double from Contreras and Pratt's sacrifice fly. Milwaukee starting pitcher Jacob Misiorowski left the game in the sixth inning and the Rays finally got on the scoreboard in the ninth as Chandler Simpson sent Liam Hicks home off a double. item.title: DeMarcus Cousins explains why Jaylen Brown has reason to feel betrayed by Celtics
item.description: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images DeMarcus Cousins has defended Jaylen Brown amid the ongoing tension between the Philadelphia 76ers star and the Boston Celtics, questioning Brian Scalabrine’s recent comments about the forward. Brown’s relationship with his former team has become a talking point after reports emerged that he wanted to leave Boston during the offseason. However, Brown’s representatives strongly denied that he had requested a trade. Former Celtics player Scalabrine initially reported that Brown had demanded a trade before later clarifying that he had “technically didn’t demand to be traded”. DeMarcus Cousins says Jaylen Brown had reason to feel unappreciated Cousins criticised Scalabrine’s approach while discussing the situation on Run It Back , suggesting the commentator was failing to consider Brown’s perspective. “I think Scal is kind of whack for this,” Cousins said. He continued: “Obviously, he has a job to do, but it’s giving homer vibes. There’s more context to this conversation than you know, he requested a trade. He didn’t feel appreciated. The team did dangle him out there in trade conversations.” Cousins also highlighted Brown’s contributions to Boston, arguing that the forward had earned greater appreciation after stepping up when another superstar was unavailable. “The year before that, I win a Conference Finals MVP. We win a championship. All these things, and what do I get in return? Now my name is being dangled in trade conversations. So after all that, yeah, I would feel a certain way too,” he added. Brown has remained complimentary of Jayson Tatum, while Tatum has repeatedly denied that there was friction between the former teammates. The situation took another turn when Brown’s team told ESPN’s Kris Rhim that the report claiming he had demanded a trade was “10000% a lie”. Despite that denial and his subsequent clarification, Scalabrine has continued making comments about Brown during Celtics broadcasts. The two teams are scheduled to meet next month, with Brown now representing Philadelphia after the 76ers acquired him from Boston in a deal involving Paul George and significant draft compensation. That first meeting could provide another chapter in a story that has continued to draw attention since the offseason. item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, FL. – The timing was just too good. Asked by a reporter if he could describe what he was feeling in the midst of the Milwaukee Brewers ' raucous clubhouse celebration at Tropicana Field following the team's 4-1 Game 5 victory that earned the franchise its first World Series crown, team principal owner Mark Attanasio couldn't help but point out the song that was blasting through the speakers only feet away. "I'm floating right now," he said, sporting the standard issue sprayware of goggles, t-shirt, shorts and flip-flops. "This is a lot to take in. World Series Game 5, you win, you're on a podium, there's like 30,000 people in the stands screaming and cheering and there's another 30,000-40,000 people at a watch party and there's probably over a million people in Wisconsin who care about this and were watching. "So, it's all sinking in. They talk about world champs, you hear the Queen song ("We Are The Champions"), and we are. You can dream about it, you can think about it and nothing compares. "Nothing compares to the experience." Get Milwaukee Brewers championship gear, books to celebrate World Series win! Only hours earlier Attanasio was making the pre-game rounds like usual on the field in front of the Brewers dugout. He was outwardly calm, but like anyone who'd watched the Brewers drop that 4-3, 12-inning heartbreaker in Game 4 a night earlier, there was undoubtedly an underlying sense of nervousness that perhaps the Rays had suddenly gained momentum. And they had ace Drew Rasmussen on the mound, albeit on short rest. As it turned out, there would be nothing to worry about. Jacob Misiorowski successfully battled iffy mound conditions for all of his 5 ⅔-inning start before departing with cramping in his right calf, the offense generated a 2-0 lead by the fifth inning and doubled it an inning later and old trusted hands Abner Uribe and Trevor Megill handled things the rest of the way to lock it down. item.description: FBL-ITA-SERIE A-MILAN-BOLOGNA - AFP AC Milan veteran Luka Modric has delivered a brutally honest assessment of the Rossoneri's first league defeat of the season, admitting that the side was caught off guard by their second-half collapse against Bologna. Despite a positive start to the campaign under new management, the Croatian midfielder acknowledged that the visitors were fully deserving of their 4-2 victory at San Siro. Milan's unbeaten start comes to a halt The Rossoneri saw their unbeaten start to the Serie A campaign shattered on Wednesday following a disappointing 4-2 home loss against Bologna. After a solid opening 45 minutes, Ruben Amorim's side fell apart in the second period and surrendered their early-season momentum. Modric was introduced into the fray at half-time, replacing the injured Fikayo Tomori. However, the 41-year-old veteran was unable to stem the tide as the visitors took complete control of the contest. The result leaves Milan sitting fifth in the league standings, having collected 18 points from their opening nine fixtures. Modric delivers brutal assessment of Bologna loss Speaking to Sky Sport Italia , Modric offered a frank evaluation of his team's second-half collapse. The Croatian midfielder acknowledged that the squad was stunned by the sudden shift in momentum. "It was a bad defeat; we didn’t expect it, especially after the first half," he admitted. "I think we had done well in the league until now, and tonight we lost our first game. We lost so many duels in the second half. That set-piece goal was unfortunate, and from that moment we threw ourselves down. We deserved to lose." Despite the setback, Modric urged his team-mates to look forward. "We have no excuses. There have been injuries, but it’s a positive that the next game is right away. We had done really well until tonight, so we must stay optimistic and hope to react on Saturday," he continued. Amorim's tactical revolution remains on track While the Bologna defeat exposes temporary frailties, the broader consensus within the Milan camp remains firmly positive. Modric, who has provided two league assists this term and is under contract until the end of the season, threw his support behind Amorim's ongoing tactical overhaul. "I think we are going the right way," the midfielder argued. "The coach has arrived with new ideas, with a new style of play, and we are trying to understand his ideas and what he asks of us." Recognising that the squad is still adapting, Modric stressed the importance of patience, adding: "As I said before, we had done well until tonight. You can always do more, but we still need to improve, and we hope to do it during the season." item.description: Galatasaray make Andre Onana transfer stance clear as Man United slap price tag Galatasaray’s position on a potential swoop for Andre Onana has emerged, even as Manchester United name their price for the goalkeeper. Galatasaray interest Onana is currently on another season-long loan at Trabzonspor. He spent last term with the Turkish club, a move that was sanctioned by then-manager Ruben Amorim. Amorim started the season with Altay Bayindir in goal before dipping into the market for Senne Lammens, who has since cemented his status as the undisputed number one. Onana briefly returned to United in the summer and is believed to have been keen on fighting for his place in the team, but he agreed to return to Trabzonspor after it became apparent that opportunities under Michael Carrick would not be forthcoming. The Cameroonian is steadily rebuilding his career after a disastrous spell at United in which he became synonymous with comical errors that proved costly to United. A recent report covered by The Peoples Person relayed that Galatasaray are admirers of Onana. It was indicated that Galatasaray were prepared to open talks with the Red Devils over a deal for the player. However, a new update has stated that Galatasaray are not in the running for Onana’s signature. Onana update According to Turkish Football , Trabzonspor are working hard to turn Onana’s loan deal into a permanent arrangement. The news outlet adds, “Trabzonspor officials remain eager to lock down the 30-year-old shot-stopper long-term, viewing him as a central pillar in their defensive setup.” “However, despite recent reports linking Galatasaray with a potential move for the keeper, the Istanbul outfit have formally declared themselves out of the race.” “RAMS Park hierarchy have opted to direct their summer transfer budget toward other priority targets and are content with their goalkeeper options.” Turkish Football add that United remain open to selling Onana, who is valued at around €18m. Onana feels settled in Trabzonspor and there is confidence that they will eventually succeed in their efforts to retain him beyond this season.
